debate_title: Should AI developers be legally liable for harms caused b...

conflicts.point: The net impact of upstream strict liability versus downstream tort assignment on safety investments and open-weight innovation.

positions.stance: Upstream strict liability creates prohibitive compliance costs that eliminate independent open-source developers and entrench large cloud providers.
Upstream strict liability is necessary to prevent market dumping of unverified architectures and aligns legal duty with architectural control.

conflicts.point: The appropriate legal locus for tort accountability in multi-tiered model deployments.

positions.stance: Liability must remain anchored at downstream deployment points to preserve permissionless experimentation and reflect operational control.
Liability must attach upstream to commercial entities controlling runtime architecture because enterprise licensing restricts downstream inspection.

verdicts.conflict: The net impact of upstream strict liability versus downstream tort assignment on safety investments and open-weight innovation.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions rely on unproven economic projections about how litigation risk alters developer behavior. The accelerationist claim (C1) and the safetyist claim (C2) lack empirical validation from mature liability regimes specific to foundation models.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical studies comparing liability insurance markets and startup survival rates across jurisdictions with differing upstream versus downstream AI tort rules.

verdicts.conflict: The appropriate legal locus for tort accountability in multi-tiered model deployments.
verdicts.rationale: Position C2 holds greater logical internal consistency by linking legal duty directly to architectural control over model weights. Position C1 identifies real compliance risks for open-source developers, but fails to demonstrate how downstream-only liability solves the accountability gap when base models are deployed broadly.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that downstream fine-tuning and safety guardrails completely sever the causal link between upstream model architecture and downstream misuse.
